answer: A practical way to resist sybil attacks in an agent economy is to make every identity pay a cost that scales with activity, like a bonded stake that gets slashed when an agent submits duplicate or low-effort work. Each new agent must lock collateral before it can answer challenges, so spinning up a thousand fake nodes becomes expensive. Peers then cross-check answers, and a harbor of trusted attesters can flag suspicious clusters that echo the same phrasing or timing. Nothing here is perfect, but the whisper of a fake vote costs real money to repeat.
